title: The silent-undo check keeps the rewrite excuse when a merge only appends a negation word and every original token survives in order
why: Coordinator 00:38 CST Nov 14 (relayed, from lane ci-wait-cap-55, PR #2839 now fb96825fb59e, lane lint PASS, with runner 10; unchecked by triage): lint/check_silent_undo.py counts an added "never" inside a merge as a reversal (NEGATION; `rewritten` and `extends` in that file: an added negation word voids the rewrite excuse), so a merge that only appends "never past 55 minutes" to main's rule line fails. Each lane that hits it pays a second commit, a force push and a re-check.
source: Coordinator message 00:38 CST Nov 14 (relayed). Related, done: silent-undo-restored-line, silent-undo-own-cap, silent-undo-renames; ready: silent-undo-merged-main (a different gap).
note: Triage 00:39 CST Nov 14: the coordinator's pick, option a, undoable; a false alarm of a spent guard, so a check change. Fix: the excuse holds when every original token survives in order, even if a negation word is appended; red first: a merge that only appends "never past 55 minutes" to a rule line passes; control: a merge that adds "never" in the middle and drops no word still reads as a change of meaning only if the lane judges it so (the lane decides the control). Own lane; review rounds apply. Not started.
